rationale: This benchmark is a small (30 functions, ~14 KB text) dense numeric eigenvalue solver (Jacobi, QR iteration, triangularization) dominated by arithmetic loops in a few large kernels (Trianglelise, Jacobi, QRiterate), so the weight table favors low-overhead arithmetic and structural transforms while constraining cost-heavy ones: SUB gets the highest applicability (high SecurityGain/DiversityGain with minimal RuntimeCost/SizeCost and near-zero CorrectnessRisk) because float/int arithmetic substitution is cheap and effective on this arithmetic-dense code; FLA gets strong SecurityGain/DiversityGain to flatten the large control-flow-heavy kernels where static analysis hurts most, but its moderate RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights keep it away from tight inner loops; BCF is kept moderate with elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost so bogus-path insertion lands on the bigger functions rather than hot numeric loops; SPLIT is favored for DiversityGain at near-zero cost since splitting basic blocks amplifies FLA/BCF effectiveness cheaply; IBR and ICALL are mid-weight with elevated CorrectnessRisk because indirect branching/calls on floating-point-heavy code with few indirect targets yield modest gains and carry the most semantic risk (function-pointer/exception-edge breakage); IGV is kept moderately applicable with low CorrectnessRisk because this code makes regular use of module-level state (grid, solution matrices, iteration counters) whose indirection meaningfully obscures dataflow at acceptable cost.
